subject: react
summary: Explains useEffect hook behavior, dependency array patterns (empty, specified, omitted), cleanup functions for resource management, and async handling including race condition prevention.
key_points: useEffect runs after render; the dependency array controls when it re-runs — empty means mount-only, specified means on-change, omitted means every render.
Cleanup functions returned from useEffect run before the next effect and on unmount — essential for timers, listeners, and connections.
The useEffect callback cannot be async directly; define an inner async function and call it instead.
misconceptions: The useEffect callback can be declared as async directly.
An empty dependency array [] means the effect runs on every render.
Omitting a dependency from the array has no consequences if the value rarely changes.
check_questions: What are the three dependency array patterns and when does each cause the effect to run?
When exactly does a cleanup function execute?
How does the cancelled flag pattern prevent race conditions in async effects?

fact_candidates: Three dependency array patterns: [] (mount), [dep] (on change), omitted (every render)
Cleanup function runs before next effect execution and on component unmount
practical_judgment_candidates: Determining which values belong in the dependency array
Identifying side effects that require cleanup (timers, event listeners, WebSocket)
error_interpretation_candidates: Infinite loop caused by omitting dependency array on an effect that calls setState
Memory leak from missing cleanup on setInterval or addEventListener
scenario_candidates: WebSocket notification counter with proper cleanup on unmount
Search component with race condition prevention using cancelled flag
common_wrong_answer_patterns: Believing useEffect callback can be async without an inner function
Assuming empty dependency array means the effect fires on every render
